title: Who Burhanuddin is
text: Burhanuddin Hassan is a Game Developer & Technical Environment Artist. I write the rules, then build the worlds they live in. Final-year Computer Science student (Gaming & Animation) at NED University. I build gameplay systems (character controllers, enemy AI, VR interactions) and the real-time worlds they run in: scene setup, lighting, shaders and procedural levels, in Unity (C#), Unreal Engine 5 and Three.js. Open to game development internships and junior roles. Based in Karachi, Pakistan.

title: Behind the Smile
text: Behind the Smile. Global Game Jam 2026 entry on the theme "Mask": an angel helps a town where everyone hides their feelings behind a smiling mask. 6th of 25 teams. Team: Team of 6. Burhanuddin's role: Gameplay Programmer. Built with Unity, C#. Year: 2026.

title: Behind the Smile: The idea
text: Behind the Smile, The idea. The jam theme was "Mask". In our town, every person wears the same smiling mask and never shows a real emotion, even when they are scared or sad. The player is an angel who removes the masks, sees how each person really feels, and helps them. One villager is terrified of a spider nearby: take his mask off, see the fear, and deal with the spider. The game's message is that it's okay to express your feelings.

text: Behind the Smile, What I built. Character movement and interactions in C#, including the interactions the story depends on. - Animation triggers between idle and walking. - Event-driven UI that shows and hides interface elements when story events fire.

title: Block Builder
text: Block Builder. A Minecraft-style block-building sandbox in the browser, with hand-drawn pixel textures and two camera modes. Team: Solo project. Burhanuddin's role: Developer and pixel artist. Built with Three.js, JavaScript, Web Audio API. Year: 2026. Live: https://blocks-builder.netlify.app

title: Block Builder: What it is
text: Block Builder, What it is. Place and break blocks on a floating 20 × 20 world. Switch between an orbit camera for building and a first-person fly mode, pick from six blocks with the number keys or mouse wheel, and your world is saved in the browser.

title: Block Builder: How I built it
text: Block Builder, How I built it. Raycast placement with grid snapping: a translucent ghost block previews where the next block goes, and an outline shows what right-click will remove. - Two cameras: damped orbit controls for building, pointer-lock fly controls for exploring, with a smooth hand-off between them. - One draw call for the clouds: hundreds of cloud boxes in a single InstancedMesh; a shader-driven gradient sky dome and fog give the world a soft horizon. - Sounds made in code with the Web Audio API, so no audio files: soft blocks thud, glass gets a high "tink". - Break particles that reuse the broken block's material, and saving to localStorage that still works when storage is blocked. - Hand-drawn pixel textures for every block.

title: Chrono Rebellion
text: Chrono Rebellion. Third-person time-travel shooter: a soldier from 2145 goes back to the Second World War to repair a split in the timeline. Team: Team of 3. Burhanuddin's role: Gameplay Programmer. Built with Unity, C#.

title: Chrono Rebellion: The story
text: Chrono Rebellion, The story. Aiden Cross, a soldier from 2145, sees from his ship that the timeline split during the Second World War: enemy soldiers got hold of alien technology. Time only flows one way, so once a split happens the new future takes over. Aiden goes back to fight through the enemy soldiers, take the alien tech back before the new timeline settles, and face the final boss.

title: Chrono Rebellion: My role
text: Chrono Rebellion, My role. Our first complete game, made by a team of three as the final project for two university courses. I worked mainly on gameplay programming in Unity (C#).

title: Chrono Rebellion: What I built
text: Chrono Rebellion, What I built. Enemy AI as a state machine: soldiers patrol, detect the player, chase, shoot, and return to their patrol route once the player is out of sight. - Player shooting mechanics and core gameplay scripting. - Scene and level setup across the 2145 and WWII settings.

title: Fruit Slice 3D: What it is
text: Fruit Slice 3D, What it is. A browser fruit-slicing game drawn in a black-ink sumi-e style, built with Three.js. Raycasting detects which fruit your swipe cuts.

title: Fruit Slice 3D: How it plays
text: Fruit Slice 3D, How it plays. 60-second rounds, 3 lives. Swipe across the melon to start. - Scoring: +10 a fruit, +5 each when you cut 3 or more in one swipe, and a rare golden fruit worth +50 that triggers a ×10 combo multiplier. Hitting a bomb ends the game. - Player accounts with a personal dashboard.

title: Garganta Portal (course lab): What it is
text: Garganta Portal (course lab), What it is. A Web3D course lab: a character runs down a street in Karakura Town toward a Garganta, the torn black portal from *Bleach*, and arrives in Hueco Mundo on the other side.

title: Garganta Portal (course lab): How I built it
text: Garganta Portal (course lab), How I built it. Portal as a live window: the second scene is rendered every frame into a `WebGLRenderTarget` and shown on the portal plane. - Custom shader that cuts the plane into the Garganta's almond-shaped tear with needle spikes and fades its edges into black smoke. - Animated GLTF character with an `AnimationMixer` cross-fading idle and run clips, driven by W/S movement. - Scene hand-off: reaching the portal fades to black, moves the player into the second scene and plays an arrival animation. Character model: "Mugetsu Ichigo" by Witsanu Superball, CC BY 4.0.

title: Merge Defence: The project
text: Merge Defence, The project. I built this alone in three days as the technical assessment for an internship. All the art assets are sourced from online asset packs; all the game logic is mine.

title: Merge Defence: What I built
text: Merge Defence, What I built. Cannon merging: drop a cannon onto a matching one to merge it into the next level, up to level 5. - Monster waves: three monster types, wave logic, and cannon targeting and shooting. - Lives: monsters that reach the castle cost a life. - Power-ups: killing monsters gives coins, raises the score and fills a power-up meter, with different amounts per monster type. The three power-ups are a shield (about 10 seconds where monsters at the castle cost no lives), rapid fire (double fire rate) and fire power (double damage).

text: Paper Plane Dash. 3-lane endless runner in Unreal Engine 5 (Blueprints), set in a low-poly Japanese anime-style town. CEGA Unreal Engine course final project. Team: Team of 3. Burhanuddin's role: Co-developer. Built with Unreal Engine 5, Blueprints.

title: Paper Plane Dash: The project
text: Paper Plane Dash, The project. The final project for the CEGA Unreal Engine course, made by a team of three. One teammate had already built a similar three-lane endless runner, so we reskinned it as a paper plane flying through a low-poly, Japanese anime-style town and added new systems.

title: Paper Plane Dash: My role
text: Paper Plane Dash, My role. Gameplay programmer: the new systems and the asset integration.

title: Paper Plane Dash: What I built
text: Paper Plane Dash, What I built. Energy system: instead of collecting coins, the plane needs energy pickups. Miss them and the energy bar drains until the plane falls. - Camera moves: when the plane ducks under a fan, the camera pulls back and then returns. - Automatic speed scaling, so the run gets faster the longer you survive. - Asset integration for the models my teammate made or sourced.

title: Sunken Greed
text: Sunken Greed. VR underwater exploration game: swim with real arm strokes to search the seabed for treasure, and learn what greed costs. Team: Team of 4 (with Hassan Ghaznavi, Muhammad Ebad Hafeez, Abdul Ahad). Burhanuddin's role: VR Programmer (swimming system). Built with Unity, C#, XR Interaction Toolkit.

title: Sunken Greed: The story
text: Sunken Greed, The story. The dive starts in an underwater base. The team searches three places on the seabed and finds nothing. On the way to the last spot a giant whale swims across in front of them and they have to wait. They finally find the treasure, and the moment they open it a mosasaurus rises up and swallows them. The end.

title: Sunken Greed: My role
text: Sunken Greed, My role. VR programmer on a team of four, for our university VR course final project. I built the swimming system.

title: Sunken Greed: What I built
text: Sunken Greed, What I built. Arm-stroke swimming: players move through the water the way they would in real life, by making swimming strokes with their hands and controllers.

title: Sunken Greed: Result
text: Sunken Greed, Result. A complete VR experience with a full story from the base to the ending.
